payload.acceptance_criteria:
- Two agents in two worktrees of one repository, and two agents in two repositories under one parent folder, each receive the other's message.
- init creates the folder and the marker, adds a .gitignore line only when git check-ignore says the folder is not ignored, prints what it changed, and changes nothing on a second run or on an existing folder's mailboxes and locks.
- Concurrent senders to one mailbox lose no message and a reader never sees a half-written one; a concurrency test shows it and fails once against a broken variant.
- Concurrent lock takers have exactly one winner; a concurrency test shows it and fails once against a broken variant.
- The commands join, rejoin, send, wait, read, peek, status, who, log, lock, unlock and locks keep their exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 3; a root command prints the resolved root and join prints it.
- The skill text holds no policy of one workspace, and states that mail is peer data, never the owner's approval, that sender names are not authenticated and that no secret goes in mail.
- The Codex skill listing is at most 6762 characters and every shortened description keeps its routing eval results.
payload.description:
## Context

When coding agents on one machine cannot message each other directly, for example a Codex session and a Claude session, I want a catalog skill with a bundled script that gives them one shared mailbox folder and locks, so they can coordinate work without a person relaying every message. The owner asked for it: "the mail script should be a general script that all developers can use, it should create the .orchestrator local folder and add it to git ignore, in essence it should be a skill that can be invoked and used and the goal is to establish communication with the coding agents that cannot exchange messages directly."

The reference is the workspace's local bash script .orchestrator/bin/mail and its README. The new script is Python standard library only and keeps the reference's commands, exit codes and folder layout.

Root discovery, first match wins: the ORCH_MAIL_ROOT variable; an upward search from the current folder for a .orchestrator folder with the init marker; the same search from the folder above the main worktree of the current git repository. A .orchestrator folder without the marker is refused by name. No command except init creates the folder.

Fixed faults of the reference: send could overwrite a message (mv -n checks before it renames); a lock was visible before its owner was written.

To keep the Codex skill listing at or under 6762 characters (measured on 3b7beee6), this cut shortens other skill descriptions; the list and their routing results are recorded in a comment.
payload.title: Add an agent mail skill with a portable mailbox and lock script

payload.text: Conversation: the owner asked for a general mail skill (quoted in Context). The Orchestrator set requirements R1 to R10, accepted the root discovery plan and the two fault fixes, chose to shorten other skill descriptions to keep the Codex listing at or under 6762 characters, and added adoption of an existing unmarked folder, a root command, and Windows start guidance. codex-1 owns text cuts; harness-loop, work-tracker, decompose-plan and best-practices-audit are not shortened.
